notes: All tuning for the ring-escape format lives here, never in code. Distances are px in the 1080x1920 frame, angles in degrees, time in seconds. Re-run `python escape/engine.py --survey 100` after editing to see how durations and per-ring timings move.

rings.notes: gap_deg is per ring, inner first; its length is the ring count. All gaps start lined up at t=0. Ring i spins at spin_deg_per_sec + spin_step * i, so the gaps slowly drift apart: early on the ball flies through several aligned rings at once, later each ring has to be escaped alone. Negative spin turns the other way. boss_push_px adds radial space before the last boss_rings rings, so they read as a final wall.

shape.notes: What engine.score() rewards: a hard slam, a long dry stretch, then the escape. burst wants at least burst_min_rings rings broken inside one burst_window_seconds window that ends by burst_deadline_seconds (the 4s budget leaves room for a later countdown). After the slam, the mean gap between breaks (the final escape included) should sit inside middle_break_interval_lo..hi seconds, and no single gap may run past silence_max_seconds. lo/hi depend on the ring count: tune.py shape_for() derives them. The last ring should hold the ball at least finale_min_seconds. Terms combine as a geometric mean; usable means score >= usable_score.
